 Let’s have a warm welcome for our brothers in football despair, the Cal Bears
 by Steven Muma Oct 30, 2026, 11:22 AM UTC Facebook 
 Link 
 DALLAS, TEXAS - OCTOBER 24: Jaron-Keawe Sagapolutele #3 of the California Golden Bears looks to pass as Marques White #16 of the SMU Mustangs pursues during the first half at Gerald J. Ford Stadium on October 24, 2026 in Dallas, Texas. (Photo by Ron Jenkins/Getty Images) Getty Images California and NC State are coming together this week for the Man, It’s REALLY Not Our Year Bowl , and there’s a decent chance this is the only bowl appearance either team will make. These two programs have basically played out the exact same season, just on opposite coasts: both have been wrecked by injuries and questionable coaching, quickly dashing high preseason hopes tied to their respective returning quarterbacks.
 New head coach Tosh Lupoi’s debut has been disheartening for Cal, to say the least. It’s one thing to struggle on the field, and a lot could be forgiven considering the injury mess, but there have been enough concerning signs elsewhere that Bears fans have been wondering if they’ve made a huge mistake with this hire.
 Lupoi brought in a pair of NFL assistants to serve as his offensive coordinator and defensive coordinator, despite neither having ever worked as a coordinator before. It turns out that having your head coach and both coordinators learning on the job all at the same time is maybe not the best idea, and OC Jordan Somerville was stripped of his play-calling duties early in October.
 Lupoi worked hard during the offseason to keep quarterback Jaron-Keawe Sagapolutele in the fold only to utterly stunt his growth with an offense that was dead on arrival in Week 1 . The 2025 version of Cal wasn’t great but it was often entertaining; this year they haven’t even had that. Mismanaging your biggest and most important talent like this is a pretty bad sign for Lupoi’s long-term prospects.
 Anyway this is the Cal offense’s advanced stats radar:
 You could treat these radars as a Rorschach test: the 2026 Cal offense is a depressed jellyfish heading into the depths of the sea, and whether it is consumed by a shark or killed by the extreme pressure of the deep, it cares not.
 This is what happens when you have bad coaching and you have so many injuries that you need to bring defensive players over to contribute at the skill positions. As I mentioned yesterday , Cal might not have its top three running backs this weekend, it might be missing two starting offensive linemen, and multiple receivers could be out, including their second-leading pass-catcher. Defensive back Niles Davis, one of three defensive players to play on offense last weekend, stepped in with four carries at running back.
 The Bears are averaging 70 rushing yards per game in league play, and 2.7 yards per carry. They have been held under 100 yards rushing in six of their seven FBS games, with a season-high of 119 rushing yards, which came against UCLA in Week 1. The running game was going to be an issue all season, the injury pile-up just made it a five-alarm fire. (Sounds familiar.)
 So Cal ain’t running the ball a whole lot these days. I’d expect JKS to throw the ball a lot again this weekend, even if he only has like two wide receivers, a ball boy, Champ the tee retriever (dog not care who throw ball, dog want ball), and a trash can on wheels serving as his receiving corps.
 Will that be enough? It could be! Because if you can lose to Stanford, you can sure as hell lose to Cal. Cal was even beating SMU at halftime last weekend … before proceeding to lose 59-20. The Bears were able to beat Virginia Tech even without JKS, though that was in Berkeley. The trips east generally don’t bode well for our new west coast pals.
 The bottom line is that I would put nothing past either of these teams, both of which are suffering from serious gunshot wounds but are capable of getting drunk enough not to notice.
